title: Transferring Visual Explainability from Self-Explaining to Prediction-Only Vision Transformers via Task Arithmetic
claim: A prediction-only model yields only logits; adding per-patch outputs from the same backbone gives explanations in a single pass.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side, bottom-to-top data flow, shared backbone with highlighted extra outputs
description: Two architecture diagrams sit side by side. The left panel, titled 'Prediction-only Vision Transformer', is a bottom-up stack. Image patches and a [CLS] token enter an orange feature extractor f_theta, marked with a flame icon for learnable. A single green CLS embedding u_0 passes into a gray domain-specific head g_w, marked with a snowflake icon for frozen, and that head outputs logits l. The patch embeddings are faded and unused. The right panel, 'Self-explaining Vision Transformer', has the same stack, but every patch embedding u_1 to u_M is brightly colored and goes into the shared head. The head outputs logits plus patch-level attributions phi_1 to phi_M, grouped by a bracket. Colors and ghosted arrows show what is newly used. A small cat photo split into patches forms the input.
caption: Model architectures of prediction-only ViT (left) and our self-explaining ViT (right). Gray boxes represent functions with fixed parameters. All the learnable parameters $\btheta$ are only in the feature extractor (filled in orange).
abstract: In image classification scenarios where both prediction and explanation efficiency are required, self-explaining models that perform both tasks in a single inference are effective. However, for users who already have prediction-only models, training a new self-explaining model from scratch is costly in both labeling and computation. This study proposes a method to transfer the visual explanation capability of self-explaining Vision Transformer (ViT) models learned in a source domain to prediction-only, zero-shot-capable ViT models based on vision-language models (VLMs) in a target domain via task arithmetic, without target-side explanation supervision. The proposed method endows target models with explanation capability by adding an explainability vector induced by explanation supervision in the source domain based on the task arithmetic framework. Experiments on 10 diverse target datasets show that a single explainability vector learned on ImageNet-1k augmented with patch-level explanation supervision transfers consistently, improving explanation quality while largely preserving classification accuracy. Within-model faithfulness evaluation and comparisons with control vectors (e.g., random vectors of the same norm) show that the transferred explanations are faithful to the model's own predictions and that the effect is specific to the explainability vector. Beyond the transfer itself, we further investigate whether transfer success can be anticipated a priori from model-internal features alone, and find that, for a fixed source, a small set of such features carries non-trivial signal about the transfer outcome on held-out targets. Code is available at https://github.com/yuyay/explainability_vector.
